title: Federal Rule 19 — required parties
summary: Rule 19 asks whether an absent person should be joined and, if joinder is not feasible, whether the action can fairly proceed without that person. The inquiry protects existing parties, absentees, and the interest in complete resolution.

sections.Role in the course: Rule 19 asks whether an absent person should be joined and, if joinder is not feasible, whether the action can fairly proceed without that person. The inquiry protects existing parties, absentees, and the interest in complete resolution.
sections.What to examine: First identify the need for the person’s participation under Rule 19(a). Then determine feasibility, including jurisdictional obstacles. If joinder is impossible, evaluate prejudice, ways to lessen it, adequacy of the judgment, and the consequences of dismissal under Rule 19(b).
